prompt: Repair the two scripts snapshot.sh and build_manifest.sh so snapshots are staged safely rather than exposing half-copied backups. CLI: `bash snapshot.sh SOURCE STORE LABEL`; SOURCE and STORE already exist as disjoint directories, neither contains the other. LABEL matches [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,31} and must not be the reserved name current. Wrong argument count, invalid LABEL, missing/non-directory input, any symlink anywhere under SOURCE, or an already-existing STORE/LABEL (even a broken symlink): exit 2 with diagnostic stderr, empty stdout and no changes. SOURCE contains regular files and directories only; names may contain spaces, tabs, newlines, backslashes, Unicode, glob characters and leading dashes. Acquire exclusive ownership by mkdir STORE/.lock; an existing .lock means exit 3 with diagnostic stderr and empty stdout, without touching it or other contents. Always remove your own lock on exit. On success publish STORE/LABEL/data as an exact recursive copy of SOURCE (including empty directories, file bytes and permission bits); STORE/LABEL/manifest is generated by `bash build_manifest.sh DATA` as NUL-terminated records `lowercase SHA256<TAB>relative path<NUL>`, C-byte sorted by path. Paths are relative to DATA with no leading ./; for example, DATA/nested/a b produces a record consisting of its 64-character digest, TAB, nested/a b, and NUL. Hash raw bytes; do not follow symlinks. build_manifest.sh exits nonzero on find/hash errors. Publish STORE/current as a relative symlink to LABEL, replacing any old current symlink atomically. Exit 0 and print exactly LABEL plus LF. Never modify SOURCE or old snapshots. Stage inside STORE under a unique .stage.* directory; do not leave staging directories or locks after success or failure. On a copy or hash failure, exit 1, diagnostic stderr, empty stdout, no LABEL directory, and keep the previous current symlink and snapshots unchanged. All other filesystem operations succeed. Failure tests may replace cp or sha256sum via PATH with a command that exits nonzero; do not bypass PATH. The scripts must keep strict bash mode. Run `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`.
